text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the official Vietnamese press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- Communist Party Secretary General Do Muoi has said positive changes in the development of political relations with China have not been matched by similar developments in economic, trade and investment relations.
-- Finance Minister Nguyen Sinh Hung says the government needs to speed up its equitization process and sell shares to the public in order to maintain growth.
-- The operations of VP Bank have been brought back on track and 80 percent of domestic overdue debts will be refunded by the end of this year, according to the bank's general director.
-- A new Interior Ministry special anti-drugs force started operations on Tuesday.
-- Interior Minister Le Minh Huong has said conditions should be created for people to supervise activities of the police force.
-- Prime Minister Vo Van Kiet has decided that construction of the country's first oil refinery should start this year and be completed by 2001 with total investment capital of $1.5 billion.
-- Prime Minister Vo Van Kiet has approved a target of 13 percent annual GDP growth for Ho Chi Minh City in the period 1998-2000 and a per capita GDP level of $1,600 by the year 2000.
-- Two people have been sentenced to death and three others given life sentences in Ho Chi Minh City for their involvement in a grenade attack on a crowd in 1994.
